notes.raw_lens: all lens readouts are the RAW J-lens: unembed(J_l @ h) with the model's own final-norm + lm_head unembedding and no bias/scale/temp/logit_bias corrections (the paper uses the raw J-lens; the calibrated variant is a separate x14/x16 path)
notes.token_form: token vectors use the form the model would emit at the readout position: ' ' + word when the preceding prompt character is not whitespace, else the bare word; the probe rank takes the MIN over both forms (the order-ops synonym convention), the swap vectors use the single emitted form
notes.scoring: answer scoring: normalize (lowercase, keep alphanumerics) both the greedy generation and the expected answer; success = the normalized generation STARTS WITH the normalized answer (covers multi-token answers like 'North America' whose stored answer is 'North')
notes.depth: depth control: the band splits into EARLY = band[:len//2] and LATE = band[len//2:]; the onset sweep walks levels shallow->deep (stride --onset-stride, deepest band layer always included) and an item's effective layer is the SHALLOWEST level whose swap flips the answer (early-stop); depth fractions are (layer - band_lo) / (band_hi - band_lo), and the paper's claim is that intermediate swaps take effect ~0.17 of depth earlier than answer swaps (i.e. a negative intermediate-minus-answer gap)
notes.onset: onset modes: 'single' edits ONLY the level's layer per level (shallowest flipping layer = effective layer); 'cumulative' edits levels[i:] (the band from the level to the band end). The EARLY/LATE half table is the primary control; the sweep is the median-effective-layer statistic
